claim: Israel runs an apartheid system in the West Bank: Palestinians live under military law, settlers under civil law, on land Israel occupies illegally.

heard.who: Michael Lynk, UN Special Rapporteur, 25 March 2022
heard.quote: a deeply discriminatory dual legal and political system that privileges the 700,000 Israeli Jewish settlers living in the 300 illegal Israeli settlements in East Jerusalem and the West Bank
Israel maintains military control over the entire area

answer: In the West Bank about 3 million Palestinians live under Israeli military law, while roughly 500,000 Israeli settlers living beside them are under Israeli civil law. Under the 1995 Oslo II accord, Israel keeps security control throughout and full control of Area C, about 60 percent. The International Court of Justice said in 2004 and again in July 2024 that the territory is occupied and that the settlements breach international law; in 2024 it called Israel's presence unlawful, by eleven votes to four. Israel says the land is disputed, not occupied. The second intifada cost over 1,000 Israeli lives, and by the Shin Bet's count suicide attacks fell from 60 in 2002 to six in the year to September 2005, after the barrier and army operations. Our reading: security does not reach the settlements, which the ICJ found unlawful, or the barrier's route, which it doubted was necessary.

Counts differ on who is included: settler figures of about 500,000 leave out East Jerusalem, which Israel annexed and where more than 200,000 settlers live; the UN counted about 465,000 settlers in the West Bank and 230,000 in East Jerusalem in 2023.

contested.text: Whether the West Bank is 'occupied'. Israel's government and scholars such as Eugene Kontorovich argue the territory was not another state's sovereign land in 1967 and that Israel's claim is the strongest; other Israeli and international legal scholars, and the ICJ twice, say it is occupied and that the law of occupation applies.

contested.text: Whether the barrier, rather than other measures, ended the suicide attacks. The INSS study dates the decline to mid-2005 after Operation Defensive Shield and the army's operations in Palestinian cities; the peer-reviewed barrier study credits the barrier; the ICJ doubted the necessity of its route.

could_not_verify: The Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics page could not be read (returns no text); Palestinian population is cited from The Week and Peace Now, which gives 'more than 3 million, 85 percent Palestinian' for the West Bank as a whole.

I did not find a readable official Israeli Foreign Ministry or Defense Ministry page for its present legal position on the West Bank, or Israel's own written statement to the ICJ; the position is cited from the Levy committee as described by the Israel Democracy Institute, from Israel Law Review, and from Netanyahu's reaction in Ynetnews and the Algemeiner. The Levy report itself is not on the card.
The percentages of Areas A, B and C (18, 21 and about 60) come from Al Jazeera and Anera; I did not find an official or World Bank page I could read, and sources vary by a point or two.

I found no readable official count of military-court conviction rates; the 'nearly 100 percent' figure is cited from The National, which itself cites Haaretz and says the army would not comment, and Israel's Justice Ministry did not provide a civilian comparison.
I did not read the full Perry et al. paper (paywalled); only the Hebrew University abstract. The Washington Institute and Israeli Foreign Ministry pages on attack counts could not be read.
The ICJ 2024 opinion's own page (node 204160) and the 2004 overview page load, but the separate-opinion pages load only through the Wayback Machine.
Reviewer: the 5,848 total in the OCHA report includes indirect deaths and is larger than the sum of its listed groups (5,315); the report's own text does not reconcile them, so the fact now says so.

Orchestrator check, 2026-11-20: the percentages for Areas A, B and C (about 18, 21 and 60 percent) are carried by one news source. The other two reliable sources on that fact are two hosts of the same accord text, which gives no percentages. The card goes back to draft until the percentages have independent support (for example UN OCHA, the World Bank or B'Tselem's maps), then to the reviewer again.
not_claimed: This card does not say the West Bank is Israeli territory or Palestinian territory; it says what the law, the court and the two sides say.
It does not say the settlements are lawful. The ICJ twice found they are not, and Israel's government rejects both opinions.
It does not say the barrier or the military courts are justified; it says why Israel gives them and what the ICJ and a peer-reviewed study found.

It does not say the second intifada excuses any act against Palestinians. The costs to Palestinians (two legal systems, unpunished settler attacks, land confiscation, displacement) are facts on this card.
It does not say the West Bank regime is apartheid. That is contested, and this card is the evidence on which the contest turns.

Israel says the land is disputed, not occupied.
The second intifada cost over 1,000 Israeli lives, and by the Shin Bet's count suicide attacks fell from 60 in 2002 to six in the year to September 2005, after the barrier and army operations.
Our reading: security does not reach the settlements, which the ICJ found unlawful, or the barrier's route, which it doubted was necessary.

skeptic.notes: Round two (re-read JVL and PA-X copies of the accord, The National, BESA, Al Jazeera, ReliefWeb, AP/Asharq Al-Awsat, The Week, OCHA, Ynet/Shin Bet, ICJ). My round-one verification was wrong on Areas A, B, C: the percentages were not in the accord. FIXED: fact 11 now carries the shares (A about 18, B 21 to 22, C about 60) with three independent readers who each give the numbers (The National 2019, BESA 2016, Al Jazeera 2019; B'Tselem via ReliefWeb is a fourth, advocacy); fact 2 is the accord's definitions; fact 10's 80 percent is carried by the American Society of International Law and VOA quoting the ICJ. Fact 2 as a record: the JVL copy is a host of the accord's text and PA-X (a second, university copy) has the same wording, so the words are right; but The National and BESA carry only the three-area split and the interim character, not the Area C definition. I trimmed 'and the divisions have persisted' (not what the record says). Weak but acceptable. NOT FIXED / NEW: [must-fix] Fact 8: the Palestinian toll (4,228), foreign (63) and 5,848 total are carried by OCHA alone; the Jerusalem Post gives 'between 2,000 and 5,000 Palestinians', which conflicts; only the 1,000-plus Israeli figure has three carriers. Mark it as a record fact with two readers who carry the figure, or state it as OCHA's count only. [must-fix] Fact 9: the numbers (60 attacks in 2002, six in the year to September 2005) come from one Shin Bet dataset repeated by Ynet and the AP (wire added, counts once); the barrier-effect, infiltration and INSS statements are separate claims. Split the fact; the numbers alone have one source. [should-fix] Fact 1 'nearly 100 percent' is one Haaretz figure via The National. Fact 0's 3-3.3 million: AP gives about 3 million for the West Bank and East Jerusalem together, The Week 3.3 million for the West Bank. Israeli lawyer: no plea-bargain context; Palestinian lawyer: barrier costs beyond the ICJ finding thin. I cannot give 'holds': two facts carry figures that one source supports.
